record.original_question: Can effective and implementable methods be developed to decide whether a rewrite system decreases with respect to some exponential interpretation, analogous to existing methods for polynomial interpretations?

evidence.quote: Develop effective methods to decide whether a system decreases with respect to some exponential interpretation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R be a finite term rewriting system over a signature Σ, where each function symbol f ∈ Σ of arity n is interpreted by a function [f] : ℕ^n → ℕ. An interpretation is called exponential if the interpretations [f] are built from constants, projections, addition, multiplication, and exponentiation x ↦ a^x (with base a ≥ 2). Each term t with variables x_1,...,x_k is then assigned a function [t] : ℕ^k → ℕ obtained by composition. The system R is said to decrease with respect to the interpretation if [ℓ](x_1,...,x_k) > [r](x_1,...,x_k) holds for all (x_1,...,x_k) ∈ ℕ^k, for every rewrite rule ℓ → r in R; this implies termination of R.

Problem: Develop an effective and implementable algorithm that, given a finite rewrite system R, decides whether there exists an exponential interpretation (in the above sense) with respect to which R decreases, analogous to the established procedures for deciding the existence of suitable polynomial interpretations. In particular, devise a mechanizable method for comparing expressions built using addition, multiplication, and exponentiation over ℕ that can serve as the core of such a decision procedure.
artifact.status_search_result: Foundational work by Lescanne and others established termination proofs via elementary (polynomial/exponential) interpretations and partial mechanization of comparison procedures, but no general effective decision method for exponential interpretations comparable to the polynomial case appears in the literature. Recent automated termination tools rely chiefly on polynomial, matrix, and related interpretations; the problem of effectively deciding decrease under exponential interpretations does not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Termination of rewrite systems by elementary interpretations
status_evidence.snippet: Termination of rewrite systems can be proved by elementary interpretations, more specifically, by functions defined by addition, multiplication and exponentiation.
status_evidence.claim: Exponential/elementary interpretations are used for termination, but a complete effective decision procedure analogous to the polynomial case is not provided.

status_evidence.title: Termination of rewriting systems by polynomial interpretations
status_evidence.snippet: Early algorithms for proving termination by polynomial interpretations have exponential complexity; methods exist for the polynomial case.
status_evidence.claim: Effective methods exist for the polynomial case, motivating the question for the exponential case, which remains without a general analogous procedure.
